literal: Means of subsistence those who lack completely not renouncing, to salt and to gruel is death.
translation: When those who lack the means to live fail to renounce the world completely, they become a deadly burden even to the salt and gruel of others.
modern: அடிப்படை வசதிகள் இல்லாதவர்கள் உலகத்தை முழுமையாகத் துறக்காமல் வாழ்வது, மற்றவர்களுடைய உப்புக்கும் கஞ்சிக்கும் எமனாக முடியும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the severe burden of extreme poverty. The word 'tuppuravu' can mean enjoyment or purity, but here it specifically refers to the basic means of subsistence. When people utterly lack these means but still cling to worldly life, they must depend on others for the barest necessities. The poet uses the striking metaphor of 'kūṟṟu' (death or the destroyer) to show that such clinging consumes and destroys even the cheap salt and sour gruel of their neighbors.
